title: BATTLE OF THE SYSTEMS: Geopolitics, 'China Shedding', Energy and AI, with Grace Shao
description: Send us Fan Mail Discover the transformative power of AI and its profound societal implications with this week's guest, Grace Shao. A distinguished writer and researcher, Grace offers unparalleled insights into global AI infrastructure, unraveling how Chinese big tech firms influence geopolitics while reshaping the global market. Get ready to explore the intriguing phenomenon of "China shedding," where Chinese tech companies strategically rebrand and relocate, often to Singapore, to appeal to international audiences. Through Grace's expertise, we unravel the complexities of Chinese tech innovation and its critical role on the world stage. We journey through the contrasting AI infrastructure capabilities of the US and China, delving into the strategic advantages China gains through its command economy. As we highlight the challenges posed by energy scarcity in the West, we also ponder the contrasting strides made by China in renewable energy. From the innovations spurred by AI to enhance energy reliability to small modular reactors' potential as a reliable energy source, this discussion promises to shed light on the intricate dynamics of the global tech competition. Join us as we critically assess the interplay of geopolitics, energy, and technology in shaping the future. We wrap up with a fascinating examination of user interface experiences across cultures, reflecting on how these design nuances shape technology satisfaction. From corporate strategies of Chinese tech firms navigating US restrictions to the evolving landscape of AI models, we cover the entire spectrum of innovation and adaptation. Debate emerges as we explore the philosophical clash between East and West, urging a shared human experience as a bridge for understanding. With a promise of thought-provoking insights and engaging discussions, this episode is a must-listen for those curious about the future of AI and its societal impact. AI Arms Race Far From Over: Chips is Only Half the Game, Infrastructure is the Other Deep Dive: Is Huawei like China’s Nvidia plus Google? Made in China AI Apps That You Are Using - Developed by ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent, Meitu, BaiChuan, MoonShot AI, Baichuan AI, MiniMax AI Learnings from East to West Bitcoin Mining for AI Data Centers? 2025 Predictions, New Year Plans for AI Proem, and Appreciation for Collaborators and Readers Release of OpenAI's o3 has completely changed the debate on whether AI scaling law has hit a wall
summary: Interview with Grace Shao (AI Pro-Am on Substack) on the US-China 'battle of the systems': energy, not GPUs, is America's real AI bottleneck while China's command economy builds data centers in weeks; the East Data West Compute policy filling poor western provinces with compute; why renewables alone can't power AI; Singapore's data-center ban birthing a Johor boom; China's open-source champion Qwen; 'China shedding' via Singaporean rebrands; and why the AI race may be won at the application layer, not the model layer.
keyTalkingPoints: Grace's Fortune op-ed thesis: the US AI bottleneck is energy - power shortages, long lead times for transformers and permits - while China's command economy rallies land, energy and labor in weeks
East Data, West Compute: data centers in poor provinces like Guizhou, Gansu and Inner Mongolia with cheap land and energy serve the urban east; data centers bring few local jobs by design

Renewables aren't a full answer: solar and wind are intermittent with limited dispatchability, and lithium batteries store hours not weeks; big tech buys renewable quotas - unfair to call it pure greenwashing, but they're not literally running on renewables; Singapore's data-center ban meanwhile birthed the Johor boom with ByteDance as biggest client, while Canada and Australia say no on citizen-burden grounds

Chips: nothing Chinese competes with Nvidia yet (Joe Tsai: at least two years behind) - but if China cracks chips, its energy advantage compounds; the winner may be decided at the application layer (Robin Li: 'the winner in AI will be an application')
Qwen is the most competitive Chinese LLM - open source, on Hugging Face and ModelScope, cheaper than Western models, with much of its developer usage outside China

Chinese consumer apps (Meitu, CapCut/Jianying, Taobao) are functionally superior - '10x the functionality' of Western equivalents; 'China shedding' sees firms rebrand as Singaporean to escape geopolitical stigma (Shein, Hill House), and Grace ends 'firmly in the middle': AI is another internet, exciting for brain-work but risky for inequality and safety

jimmy: Energy, not GPUs, is the binding constraint on US AI - and AI might one day help solve nuclear fusion
Finished, advertised commercial applications like ElevenLabs conversational AI are the next big wave, not raw models
He uses Chinese LLMs daily for translation and sees the application layer, not the model layer, as the real battleground
matt: He uses Tongyi/Qwen daily but distrusts Chinese consumer models' answers - one weird hypermolar verdict soured him on Tongyi
China's UX-maximalist super-apps are genuinely superior for image and video editing - 'far superior to anything I've seen from Western apps'
The US-China AI contest is an arms race where energy is China's trump card; the US needs permitting reform, not just chip controls
